text:
Priya: Quick heads-up — piloting a lightweight shared-channel handoff pattern I'm calling 'rippleflow' for partner SEVs (marketplace + HW + SI). Want to run a dry-run this Friday 12:30pm PST. Goal: reduce noisy duplicate bridges and make partner ownership transitions explicit. Anyone able to join?
Jared: I can join the dry-run. curious what the minimal signals are to trigger the ripple.
Priya: great — minimal signals: 1) partner channel alert (pager or ops msg) 2) bridge request via /call-bridge in shared channel 3) partner liaison confirms ownership. after that SRE oncall takes bridge for triage, partner stays for customer context.
Lian: can we codify that into a 1-paragraph checklist? easier to train partners.
Tom: +1 for checklist. also suggest we add a fallback when the partner liaison is >15m delayed: automatic escalation to partner slack + phone and fallback model endpoint (if relevant).
Priya: here's a quick checklist draft (will refine in repo after dry-run):
```
- Detect: partner-alert in shared channel or SI webhook
- Signal: partner pings `@redwood-oncall` + `/call-bridge` in-channel
- Acknowledge: partner liaison (or partner PM) replies "taking" within 5m
- Bridge: SRE joins bridge as "triage owner"; partner liaison adds customer context
- Handoff: once triage complete, SRE marks "handoff_completed" and hands control back to partner channel for postmortem
- Fallback: if no partner ack in 15m, escalate to partner exec + open secondary bridge and notify Redwood Dedicated oncall
```
Jared: nit: maybe shorten the ack window to 3m for high-severity. otherwise LGTM. :thumbsup:
Lian: calendar conflict for me Friday 12:30 — can we do 1:00pm PST? also, I'll invite one HW partner engineering contact so they see the flow.
Priya: 1:00pm PST works. updated in thread. I'll prepare a short script for the dry-run and share it here.
PartnerOpsBot: Reminder: Dry-run scheduled Fri 2026-03-27 13:00 PST — auto-invite sent to attendees and partner contact (link: https://calendar.redwood/test-dryrun).
Tom: during the dry-run let's exercise two scenarios: (A) partner-ack fast, smooth handoff; (B) partner-unavailable -> fallback escalation. want to time each step so we can set SLA knobs.
Priya: good plan. volunteers to be SRE triage owner for scenario A/B?
Jared: I'll take scenario A.
Lian: I'll coordinate partner side for scenario B and simulate delayed ack.
Tom: I'll own timing and note-taking + post-dry-run checklist (doc + action items).
Priya: amazing, thanks all. I'll post the final play checklist here after the run. tagging @channel the partners once it's checked. :white_check_mark:
Jared: thanks — curious to see latency of handoff in practice.
Lian: adding short blurb for partners on what they should expect after handoff (postmortem timeline, slack-only vs bridge notes).
Tom: also propose adding a small template message for partners to paste into the bridge to speed context transfer (customer, last-known-state, repro steps).
Priya: yup — we'll include that template in the doc. ok, see you Fri 1:00pm PST.
PartnerOpsBot: Dry-run results template will be auto-posted after the meeting.
